title: Pavement Markings, Words
summary: Standard letter layouts for the word pavement markings LANE, CLEAR, BIKE, ONLY, NO, KEEP, BUS, FWY, EXPRS, TRAIL, HOV, NORTH, SOUTH, EAST and WEST, each drawn 8'-0" tall on a 4 in. grid with its width and area. A table lists square footage per word and a detail shows the 1 ft high NO PARKING stencil.
description:
Letter layouts: all fifteen word markings are drawn as elongated outline letters on a 4 in. grid. Every word is 8'-0" tall. The width and area (A) of each word are: LANE 6'-4" wide, A=24 ft2. CLEAR 8'-0" wide, A=27 ft2. BIKE 5'-4" wide, A=21 ft2. ONLY 6'-0" wide, A=22 ft2. NO 3'-0" wide, A=14 ft2 (letters stacked side by side in a narrow block). KEEP 6'-4" wide, A=24 ft2. BUS 4'-8" wide, A=20 ft2. FWY 4'-8" wide, A=16 ft2. EXPRS 8'-0" wide, A=30 ft2. TRAIL 7'-0" wide, A=23 ft2. HOV 4'-8" wide, A=18 ft2. NORTH 8'-0" wide, A=31 ft2. SOUTH 8'-0" wide, A=29 ft2. EAST 6'-4" wide, A=22 ft2. WEST 6'-4" wide, A=24 ft2. The sheet is arranged in three rows: LANE, CLEAR, BIKE, ONLY, NO in the first row, KEEP, BUS, FWY, EXPRS, TRAIL in the second, and HOV, NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, WEST in the third.

Word Markings table: a three-column table of item and square footage (SQFT). LANE 24, CLEAR 27, BIKE 21. ONLY 22, NO 14, KEEP 24. BUS 20, FWY 16, EXPRS 30. TRAIL 23, HOV 18, NORTH 31. SOUTH 29, EAST 22, WEST 24. Bottom row: NO PARKING 2.

NO PARKING detail: the words NO and PARKING are drawn as stencil style letters on a 1 in. grid style layout, NO on a first line and PARKING on a second line below it. NO is 1'-1 1/2" wide and 1'-0" high. PARKING is 3'-9" wide and 1'-0" high. A 1 1/2" dimension marks the letter stroke or bridge width and a 2" dimension marks the gap between the two lines. A=2 ft2. The detail refers to Notes 5 and 6.
notes:
1. If a message consists of more than one word, it must read "UP", i.e., the first word must be nearest the driver.
2. The space between words must be at least four times the height of the characters for low speed roads, but not more than ten times the height of the characters. The space may be reduced appropriately where there is limited space because of local conditions.
3. Minor variations in dimensions may be accepted by the Engineer.
4. Portions of a letter, number, or symbol may be separated by connecting segments not to exceed 2 in. in width.
5. The words "NO PARKING" pavement marking is to be used for parking facilities. For typical locations of markings, see Standard Plans A90A and A90B.
6. The words "NO PARKING" shall be painted in white letters no less than 1'-0" high on a contrasting background and located so that it is visible to traffic enforcement officials.

title: Pavement Markings, Crosswalks
summary: Plan views of the higher visibility crosswalk patterns: continental, triple four, ladder and diagonal, plus the basic crosswalk of two parallel lines. Dimensions give bar widths, gaps, minimum crosswalk width and offsets from the limit line. Notes require spaces in wheel tracks, limit spacing, and white marking except yellow near schools.
description:
Continental: a row of long narrow rectangular bars set perpendicular to the direction of the crosswalk, with the bars' long dimension in the direction of pedestrian travel. Bar length is 6'-0" minimum. Bar width is dimensioned 1'-0" to 2'-0". The space between bars is dimensioned 1'-0" to 5'-0" (see Note 2). Labeled see Note 1 (spaces between markings placed in wheel tracks).

Triple Four: a pattern of rectangular blocks, each 2'-0" wide and 4'-0" long, laid out in two rows along the crosswalk, with the 4'-0" long block of the first row, a 4'-0" gap, and the 4'-0" long block of the second row (three 4'-0" dimensions stacked in the direction of travel, 12'-0" overall). Blocks within a row are 2'-0" wide with a 2'-0" minimum space between them. Block spacing across the crosswalk is 1'-0" to 5'-0" (see Note 2). Labeled see Note 1.

Ladder: two parallel transverse lines bounding the crosswalk with bars set between them parallel to the direction of travel. The crosswalk is 6'-0" minimum wide between the transverse lines, and each transverse line is 1'-0" to 2'-0" wide. The bars are spaced 1'-0" to 5'-0" apart (see Note 2) and the bar width is 1'-0" to 2'-0". Break lines show that the pattern continues across the roadway.

Diagonal: two parallel transverse lines with diagonal bars at 45 degrees between them. Crosswalk width is 6'-0" minimum, transverse lines are 1'-0" to 2'-0" wide, the diagonal bar width is 1'-0" to 2'-0", and the space between diagonal bars is 1'-0" to 5'-0" (see Note 2). The angle shown is 45 degrees.

Basic: two parallel transverse lines, each 1'-0" to 2'-0" wide, spaced 6'-0" minimum apart (clear distance), with break lines showing it continues across the roadway.

The group of Continental, Triple Four, Ladder and Diagonal is titled Higher Visibility Crosswalks.
notes:
1. Spaces between markings must be placed in wheel tracks of each lane.
2. Spacings not to exceed 2.5 times width of longitudinal line.
3. All crosswalk markings must be white except those near schools must be yellow.

title: Pavement Markings, Yield Lines, Limit Lines and Wrong Way Details
summary: Wrong way countermeasures at freeway exit ramps: a Type V arrow with red retroreflective Type R markers, and yield line and limit (stop) line layouts shown with non-recessed and recessed Type R markers. Marker spacing, offsets and Type R marker dimensions are given. A note places Type R markers in front of the first line when there is a crosswalk at the ramp end.
description:
Type V arrow at exit ramp: a long narrow arrow stem 1'-0" wide (shown with 2" offsets each side of the centerline to the markers) ending in a Y shaped head formed by two diverging legs. The arrow is A=33 ft2. The tip of the arrow is 24'-0" from the base end. The head legs are each 9'-0" long and 1'-0" wide, with a 2'-0" overall stem width at the junction. Type R markers are placed in pairs along both sides of the stem at 4'-0" on center (O/C) typical, starting from the base, with the marker rows 2" each side of the centerline. Dimensions up the stem from the base are 12'-0", 17'-6" and 24'-0", with a 2" dimension at the stem top and at the arrow tip. A note on the drawing says when recessed, use one marker at this location (at the tip). A single marker sits at the tip and a pair at the junction of the head.

Yield line at exit ramp (markers are not recessed): a row of white isosceles triangles (a series) pointing in the direction of the approaching vehicle, each 2'-0" wide at the base and 3'-0" long, spaced 1'-0" apart (typical). A Type R marker, with a red reflective face and blank back, is mounted 2" (typical) above the base of each triangle, aimed with the marker faces at 45 degrees each side of the centerline. The row is shown with a direction of travel arrow.

Yield line at exit ramp (markers are recessed): the same row of white isosceles triangles, 2'-0" wide at the base (typical), 3'-0" long (typical), spaced 1'-0" apart (typical). A row of single Type R markers is placed 3'-0" (typical) beyond the triangle base, one marker aligned with each triangle, with the marker faces red reflective and blank. Triangle series is described as white series of isosceles triangles.

Limit line (stop line) at exit ramp (markers are not recessed): a white limit line 1'-0" to 2'-0" wide (limit line or crosswalk), with Type R markers placed 2" (typical) in front of the line at 4'-0" (typical) spacing. Each marker has the faces set at 45 degrees each side, red reflective and blank.

Limit line (stop line) at exit ramp (markers are recessed): a 1'-0" white line with a row of single Type R markers placed 3'-0" (typical) from the line at 4'-0" (typical) spacing.

Yield line: a plain row of white isosceles triangles, each 2'-0" wide and 3'-0" long (typical) with 1'-0" spacing (typical).

Limit line (stop line): a single white transverse line 1'-0" to 2'-0" wide with break lines.

Type R marker details: a plan and a side profile of the marker. The marker is 3 7/8 in. to 4 1/2 in. long by 1 7/8 in. to 4 1/8 in. wide (as dimensioned: 3 7/8"-4 1/2" and 1 7/8"-4 1/8") and 3/8 in. to 3/4 in. high. A hatched area shows the retroreflective face on the backside.

Legend: a square marker symbol means Type R one-way red retroreflective marker.
notes:
Legend: Type R one-way red retroreflective marker (symbol shown).
1. If there is crosswalk at the end of the exit ramp, place Type R markers in front of the first line for wrong way vehicle that travels up the ramp with the red reflective side facing the intersection.

title: Pavement Markings, Arrows
summary: Dimensioned arrow layouts on a 1 ft grid: the Type IX U-turn arrow and the Type FH I through V combination and circular lane-use arrows. Each arrow gives overall length, width, arrowhead size and area in square feet.
description:
Type IX arrow (U-turn arrow): a U shaped arrow with the head pointing down on the left leg. Overall width 7'-9", head width 3'-4", overall height 10'-0", arrowhead 5'-0" long, right leg stem extends 8'-6" below the top of the curve, stem width 1'-0". Grid is 1'-0". A=26 ft2.

Type FH I arrow: a combination arrow with a straight through arrow, a left turn arrowhead and a right turn arrowhead, sharing one stem with an oval void. Overall width 11'-0", through arrowhead width 3'-4", overall height 19'-4", through arrowhead 5'-0" long, left and right arrowheads each have 3'-0" and 4'-0" length dimensions at the tips, stem width 1'-0". Grid is 1'-0". A=50 ft2.

Type FH II arrow: a through arrow plus a left turn arrowhead. Overall width 7'-4", through arrowhead width 3'-4", overall height 19'-4", through arrowhead 5'-0" long, left arrowhead 3'-0" and 4'-0", stem width 1'-0". Grid is 1'-0". A=38 ft2.

Type FH IV arrow: a left turn curved arrow. Overall width 7'-4", height 13'-0", arrowhead 3'-0" and 4'-0", stem 1'-0" wide. Grid is 1'-0". A=28 ft2.

Type FH III arrow (optional lane use circular arrows): a through arrowhead and a right turn arrowhead sharing a stem with an oval void. Overall width 7'-6", through arrowhead width 3'-4", height 16'-8", through arrowhead 5'-0" long, right arrowhead 3'-0" and 4'-0", stem width 1'-0". Grid is 1'-0". A=35 ft2.

Type FH V arrow (mandatory lane use circular arrows): a through arrow whose stem shifts right around an oval void. Overall width 3'-10", head width 3'-4", height 16'-8", arrowhead 5'-0" long, stem width 1'-0". Grid is 1'-0". A=23 ft2.

The arrows FH I to FH V are labeled by type: FH III is optional lane use circular arrows and FH V is mandatory lane use circular arrows.

title: Pavement Markings, Speed Measurement
summary: Plan view of white transverse speed measurement bars placed in the shoulder every mile for aircraft speed enforcement, with the R48-2 (CA) sign and a Detail A of the white X marking. A note adds an X at each end of the section if the bars are less than 1 mile apart.
description:
Plan: a roadway shown with a dashed lane line or centerline, the edge of traveled way (ETW) line and the edge of shoulder (ES) line, with an arrow showing the direction of travel. In the shoulder, between the ETW and ES lines, white transverse bars are placed that span the shoulder and are paired with a white X pavement marking just ahead of each bar. Successive bars are spaced 1 MILE apart. A dimension reads IF LESS THAN 1 MILE, SEE NOTE 1 for the section length between markings. A circle calls out Detail A at one X and bar. A sign symbol on the right shoulder at the start of the section is Sign R48-2 (CA), a vertical sign reading SPEED ENFORCED BY AIRCRAFT.

Detail A: the shoulder bar is a 12 in. white line (marked 12" WHITE) running transversely across the shoulder 6'-0" long from the ETW to the ES line side (dimension 6'-0"), with an X marking next to it. The X is 3'-0" wide and 2'-0" high, made of 4 in. white lines (marked 4" WHITE). The X is placed 1'-0" away from the bar, with a 3'-0" dimension for the X width, 1'-0" gap, and the 12 in. bar. Also shown is the ETW line (4 in. white, labeled 4" WHITE at the ETW) and the ES line.
notes: 1. Install white "X" pavement marking at each end of the section if the markings are less than 1 mile apart.

title: Pavement Markings, Bicycle Obstruction Markings
summary: Plan views of the flying wedge stripe, a tapered shoulder stripe that guides cyclists around a rumble strip or an obstruction such as a pier, abutment or grate. The taper length is L=WS (W offset in feet, S bicycle approach speed in mph), or L=(W+1)S for a raised obstruction. Use only with 5'-0" of clear space.
description:
Flying wedge stripe, placed at beginning of rumble strip at right shoulder only: a plan of the shoulder between the edge of traveled way (ETW) and the edge of shoulder (ES), with an edgeline stripe along the ETW. The rumble strip appears as a row of small rectangular elements at the upstream end next to the ETW. The flying wedge stripe is a long thin black wedge drawn from the rumble strip start, offset W from the ETW (W marked at the start of the wedge), tapering back to the edgeline over a taper length L (see Note 1). Detail 39 is referenced (see Note 3). The direction of bicycle travel arrow points toward the wedge start end. Break lines indicate the layout continues.

Flying wedge stripe, placed at obstruction: a plan of the shoulder between ETW and ES with an obstruction (pier, abutment, grate, or other obstruction that is inappropriate for bicycle travel) shown as a rectangle against the ES line, offset width W. The flying wedge stripe starts beside the obstruction at offset W and tapers to the edgeline stripe over length L (see Notes 1 and 2). See Note 3 for the stripe detail. The direction of bicycle travel arrow is shown, with break lines at the end.
notes:
1. L=WS, where W is the offset in feet and S is bicycle approach speed in mph.
2. Provide an additional foot of offset for a raised obstruction and use the formula L=(W+1)S for the taper length.
3. See Standard Plan A20D for Detail 39.
4. Use markings only when there is 5'-0" of clear space.

title: Pavement Markings, Speed Reduction
summary: Plan of transverse speed reduction pavement markings placed in the lanes with progressively closer spacing, and the three contrast treatment details that add a 2 in. black border around the white bars. The Engineer sets exact location, length and spacing based on approach and target speeds.
description:
Contrast treatment details: three small plan details, each showing a black rectangle with 2 in. contrast treatment around it. Detail 25 at the edge of traveled way (ETW): the pavement marking is 12 in. wide by 18 in. long (12" and 18" dimensions), set against the ETW line, with a 2" contrast treatment on the sides and ends. Detail 12A at a lane line (LL): the pavement marking is 12 in. wide and 36 in. long, centered on the lane line, with 18" each side of the line and a 2" contrast treatment Typ around the mark. Detail 27B at the ETW: the pavement marking is 12 in. wide by 18 in. long set against the ETW, with the 2" contrast treatment. Arrows show direction of travel.

Plan: a four lane roadway (two lanes each direction) with edge lines (ETW) and a double center line. In the upper pair of lanes, short transverse bars (pavement markings) are placed across the lanes at the ETW edges and at the lane line, with a spacing that gets progressively closer in the direction of travel (arrows pointing left). The lane line dashes continue between the bars. The lower pair of lanes shows the opposite direction (arrows pointing right) with only the dashed lane line and no bars. The bars at the lane line are drawn longer than those at the ETW edges, and where a bar meets a lane line dash a cross appears.
notes:
1. Exact location for speed reduction pavement markings will be determined by the Engineer.
2. Do not cover pavement markings.
3. Speed reduction markings are white. Contrast treatment is black.
4. Engineer to determine length and spacing based on approach and target speeds in the field.
Legend: arrow symbol means direction of travel.

title: Curb Ramp Details
summary: Plan views of curb ramp Cases A through G, typical one-ramp and two-ramp corner installations (Details A and B), Sections A-A, B-B and C-C, the detectable warning surface truncated dome geometry and the gutter pan transition. Maximum slopes are 7.5% on the ramp, 1.5% on landings and 9.0% on flares at the curb, with 4'-2" minimum landings.
description:
Case A: plan of a perpendicular curb ramp with a flare on each side and a landing behind the ramp. The sidewalk landing is 4'-2" Min long with 1.5% Max slope in both directions. The ramp width is 4'-2" Min with 1.5% Max cross slope. The ramp slope is 7.5% Max. Flares slope at 9.0% Max at the curb. The detectable warning surface (see Note 10) lies at the bottom of the ramp at the back of curb. Gutter not shown. Section A-A is cut through the ramp.

Case B: ramp with a retaining curb at the back of sidewalk. The ramp is 5'-0" Min wide, with 1.5% Max cross slope, the sidewalk beside the ramp sloping 7.5% Max toward the ramp and 1.5% Max along the sidewalk, flares at 9.0% Max at curb, and a 4'-2" Min landing. A 6" Min high retaining curb is at the edge of the sidewalk, with 6" Typ offset. Section B-B is cut through the ramp.

Case C: sidewalk depressed longitudinally. The ramp is 5'-0" Min wide with 1.5% Max cross slope, sidewalks each side at 7.5% Max sloping toward the ramp and 1.5% Max longitudinal, with no flares. The curb matches ramp slope (curb to match ramp slope). A 6" Min high retaining curb is shown at the edge of the sidewalk, 6" Typ. Section C-C is cut through the ramp.

Case D: Case A widened where distance from curb to back of sidewalk is short: the ramp widens with 1:1 Typ side transitions up to the 4'-2" Min landing, with 9.0% Max flares at the curb, 1.5% Max slopes and 7.5% Max ramp slope. A 4'-2" Min ramp width.

Case E: ramp with a flare on one side and a retaining curb on the other side, with a planting area behind. The flare is 9.0% Max at curb and the front edge of sidewalk is noted. A 6" Typ and a 4'-2" Min ramp width are shown. Retaining curb on both sides of ramp is called out where the planting area is.

Case F: ramp between two planting areas with retaining curbs on both sides of the ramp, no flares. 1.5% Max ramp cross slope, 7.5% Max ramp slope, 4'-2" Min width and 6" Typ curb.

Case G: ramp with a flare on one side and a retaining curb on the other, with planting area behind (see Note 4). Flare slope 9.0% Max at curb, retaining curb at the ramp side, 4'-2" Min width, 6" Typ curb.

Detail A, typical two-ramp corner installation (see Note 1): plan of a corner with two perpendicular ramps, one on each leg of the curb return. Each ramp has a RAMP area with detectable warning surface, a flare on each side, and a landing behind. A crosswalk if provided is shown on each leg.

Detail B, typical one-ramp corner installation (see Notes 1 and 3): plan of a corner with one diagonal ramp at the center of the curb return with flares on both sides and a landing behind it. The ramp is 4'-2" Min along its length. Crosswalk if provided. Where a flared side occurs, provide 2'-0" Min of curb.

Section A-A: gutter flowline (see Note 8), a ramp sloping 7.5% Max from the top of the ramp (rounded) down to the gutter, a landing 4'-2" Min at 1.5% Max, and thickness T.

Section B-B: gutter flowline, rounded top of ramp, ramp 7.5% Max, landing 4'-2" Min at 1.5% Max, retaining curb if necessary, thickness T. Depress entire sidewalk as required.

Section C-C: gutter flowline, a continuous 1.5% Max slope path from the gutter to the retaining curb if necessary, with thickness T.

Raised truncated dome: a side view and plan of one dome. Top diameter 0.45" Min and 0.47" Max. Base diameter 0.9" Min and 0.92" Max. Height 0.2".

Raised truncated dome pattern (in-line): domes placed in a square grid with 2.3" Min and 2.4" Max center to center spacing, Typ.

Detectable warning surface: see Note 10.

Gutter pan transition: a plan strip showing curb at the top, typical gutter pan applies to all cases at each end, a 3'-0" Typ transition (see Note 9) on each side, and between them the gutter in front of the detectable warning surface (see Note 8), with pavement below.
notes:
1. As site conditions dictate, Case A through Case G curb ramps may be used for corner installations similar to those shown in Detail A and Detail B. The case of curb ramps used in Detail A do not have to be the same. Case A through Case G curb ramps also may be used at mid block locations, as site conditions dictate. For specific site condition configuration, including the conform to existing sidewalk, see Project Plans.
2. If distance from curb to back of sidewalk is too short to accommodate ramp and 4'-2" platform (landing) as shown in Case A, the sidewalk may be depressed longitudinally as in Case B or C or may be widened as in Case D.
3. When ramp is located in center of curb return, crosswalk configuration must be similar to that shown for Detail B.
4. As site conditions dictate, the retaining curb side and the flared side of the Case G ramp shall be constructed in reversed position.
5. The ramp portion of the curb ramp is a typical rectangle, unless modified in the Project Plans.
6. Side slope of ramp flares vary uniformly from a maximum of 9.0% at curb to conform with longitudinal sidewalk slope adjacent to top of the ramp, except in Case C and Case F.
7. The adjacent surfaces at transitions at curb ramps to walks, gutters, and streets shall be at the same level.
8. Counter slopes of adjoining gutters and road surfaces immediately adjacent to and within 24 inches of the curb ramp shall not be steeper than 1V:20H (5.0%). Gutter pan slope shall not exceed 1" of depth for each 2'-0" of width.
9. Transition gutter pan slope from 1" of depth for each 2'-0" of width to match typical gutter pan slope per Standard Plan A87A.
10. The detectable warning surface will be a rectangle as shown at back of curb, unless modified in the Project Plans. Curb ramps shall have a detectable warning surface that extends the full width and 3'-0" depth of the ramp. Detectable warning surfaces shall extend the full width of the ramp except a maximum gap of 1 inch is allowed on each side of the ramp.
11. Sidewalk and ramp thickness "T", shall be 3 1/2" minimum.
12. Utility pull boxes, manholes, vaults and all other utility facilities within the boundaries of the curb ramp will be relocated or adjusted to grade by the owner prior to, or in conjunction with, curb ramp construction.
13. Detectable warning surface may have to be cut to allow removal of utility covers while maintaining detectable warning width and depth.

title: Curb Ramp and Island Passageway Details
summary: Curb ramp Cases CM and CH for ramps at raised islands, Section A-A and B-B, and Type A, B and C island passageways with detectable warning surfaces. Passageways slope 1.5% Max to drain, are 4'-2" Min wide, and need detectable warnings 2'-0" or 3'-0" deep depending on passageway length.
description:
Case CM curb ramp: plan of a curb ramp with a curved (BCR, beginning of curb return) front and detectable warning surface (see Note 2) wrapping the curved corner, with crosswalk if provided. The ramp is 5'-0" Min wide if crosswalk provided with 1.5% Max cross slope and 7.5% Max slope, with 3'-0" Typ dimension at the ramp. A 6" Min high retaining curb is at the edge of the sidewalk, 6" Typ, and if necessary, retaining curb is constructed at the edge of sidewalk. The curb matches the ramp slope. Gutter not shown. Section A-A is cut through the ramp.

Case CH curb ramp: plan of a straight ramp 5'-0" Min wide with 1.5% Max cross slope and 7.5% Max slope for the sidewalk side and 1.5% Max, with required curb on one side and a 6" Min high retaining curb. A transition from full height to zero height curb occurs over a 1'-0" dimension at the ramp. The detectable warning surface (see Note 2) is at the face of curb. If necessary, construct retaining curb at edge of sidewalk, 6" Typ. Curb to match ramp slope. Crosswalk if provided. Section A-A is cut through the ramp.

Section A-A: retaining curb if necessary at the high end, a 1.5% Max ramp slope sloping to the gutter flowline, thickness T, and gutter (see Note 7).

Section B-B: a cut through an island passageway: clear passageway between two retaining curbs, each 6" Typ, with the clear width 4'-2" Min, surface of raised island at a variable (Var) height above the passageway and thickness T.

Type A passageway: plan of a straight island passageway through a raised island between two traveled ways, with a curb ramp (see Note 7) on the sidewalk at each side. The raised island is 6'-0" Min wide. A detectable warning surface (see Notes 2 and 8) is placed at each side of the passageway, with the passageway 4'-2" Min wide, sloped to drain 1.5% Max. Dimension See Note 3 marks the detectable warning depth.

Type B passageway: plan of a raised island with an angled (bent) passageway: the passageway enters from one side and exits diagonally, with a detectable warning surface (see Notes 2 and 8) at each end, each 4'-2" Min wide, and sloped to drain 1.5% Max. A curb ramp (see Note 7) is at the adjacent corner. See Note 3 for detectable warning depth.

Type C passageway: plan of a triangular raised island with a passageway that has detectable warning surfaces (see Notes 2 and 8) on three sides: two at the entry and exit ends and one on the diagonal side, each 4'-2" Min wide, with passageway sloped to drain 1.5% Max. See Note 3.
notes:
1. Sidewalk, ramp and passageway thickness "T", shall be 3 1/2" minimum.
2. For details of detectable warning surfaces, see Standard Plan A88A.
3. Where an island passageway length is greater than or equal to 6'-0", but less than 8'-0", each detectable warning surface shall extend the full width and 2'-0" depth of the passageway length. Where an island passageway length is greater than or equal to 8'-0", each detectable warning surface shall extend the full width and 3'-0" depth of the passageway length. Detectable warning surfaces shall extend the full width of the island passageway except a maximum gap of 1" is allowed on each side of the passageway.
4. The adjacent surfaces at transitions at curb ramps to walks, gutters, and streets shall be at the same level.
5. Utility pull boxes, manholes, vaults and all other utility facilities within the boundaries of the curb ramp will be relocated or adjusted to grade by the owner prior to, or in conjunction with, curb ramp construction.
6. Detectable warning surface may have to be cut to allow removal of utility covers while maintaining detectable warning width and depth.
7. For additional curb ramp details, see Standard Plan A88A.
8. The detectable warning surface will be a rectangle as shown at the face of curb, unless modified in the Project Plans.

title: Accessible Parking Off-Street
summary: Plan layouts of off-street accessible parking: a single stall, a double stall and diagonal double stalls, each with a 5'-0" Min or 8'-0" Min van access aisle, blue bordered aisle with white diagonals, and ISA markings. Table A gives required accessible stall counts, and the sheet shows the ISA marking and the R99, R99C, R99B, R7-8b and R100B(CA) signs.
description:
Single parking stall: a regular accessible stall with a 9'-0" Min wide stall beside an access aisle that is 5'-0" Min wide for a regular accessible stall or 8'-0" Min for a van accessible stall (see Notes 2, 11, and 12). The stall is 18'-0" Min long (Typ) and bounded by 4" white lines. The aisle is bordered by 4" blue line borders with 4" white line diagonals at 3'-0" Max centers (see Note 8). A curb or bumper (see Note 3) is shown at each stall at the rear, and a 2'-0" Min unobstructed area is kept at the sidewalk end. An ISA marking is at the rear limit of the stall (see Detail A). A curb ramp (see Note 7) with retaining curb if necessary connects the aisle to the sidewalk, and ISA parking signs (see Notes 2 and 13) stand at the sidewalk. The words NO PARKING (see Note 9) are at the bottom of the aisle. A regular non-accessible parking stall is shown beside the aisle.

Double parking stall: two 9'-0" Min (Typ) wide stalls on each side of a shared access aisle, with 18'-0" Min (Typ) stall length. The aisle has 4" blue borders and 4" white diagonals at 3'-0" Max centers (see Note 8), a 2'-0" Min unobstructed area, bumpers (see Note 3), ISA markings at the rear limit of each stall, and NO PARKING in the aisle (see Note 9). The aisle is 5'-0" Min between regular accessible parking stalls and 8'-0" Min to the right of each van accessible parking stall (see Notes 2 and 12). A curb ramp (see Note 7) and ISA parking signs (see Note 13, and Notes 2 and 13) are at the sidewalk.

Diagonal double parking stalls: two angled stalls, 18'-0" Min (Typ) long and 9'-0" Min (Typ) wide, either side of a shared angled access aisle with 4" blue line borders and 4" white line diagonals at 3'-0" Max centers (Typ, see Note 8). Each stall has a 4" white line, an ISA marking at the rear limit (Typ, see Detail A), a bumper (see Note 3, Typ) with 2'-0" unobstructed dimension, and NO PARKING in the aisle (see Note 9). The aisle is 5'-0" Min between regular accessible parking stalls and 8'-0" Min to the right of each van accessible parking stall (see Notes 2 and 12). A curb ramp (see Note 7), retaining curb if necessary, and ISA parking signs (see Notes 2 and 13) are at the curb.

Detail A, ISA marking: a square blue background with a white border and a white International Symbol of Accessibility. See Standard Plan A24C for the ISA marking.

Table A: minimum number of required accessible parking spaces by total number of parking spaces provided in the parking facility. 1 to 25 spaces: 1. 26 to 50: 2. 51 to 75: 3. 76 to 100: 4. 101 to 150: 5. 151 to 200: 6. 201 to 300: 7. 301 to 400: 8. 401 to 500: 9. 501 to 1000: 2 percent of total. 1001 and over: 20 plus 1 for each 100 or fraction thereof over 1000.

Off-street parking signs (parking lot or garage, see Note 6): Sign R99(CA), a vertical sign with the ISA and the words PARKING ONLY. Sign R99C(CA), the same sign with a MINIMUM FINE $250 panel below (see Note 6). Plaque R99B(CA), reading MINIMUM FINE $250, used with Sign R99(CA) (see Note 6). Sign R7-8b reading VAN ACCESSIBLE (see Notes 2 and 6). Sign R100B(CA), a rectangular sign reading: UNAUTHORIZED VEHICLES PARKED IN DESIGNATED ACCESSIBLE SPACES NOT DISPLAYING DISTINGUISHING PLACARDS OR SPECIAL LICENSE PLATES ISSUED FOR PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES WILL BE TOWED AWAY AT THE OWNER'S EXPENSE. TOWED VEHICLES MAY BE RECLAIMED AT (Insert Address) OR BY TELEPHONING (Insert Telephone Number) (see Note 10).
notes:
1. Accessible parking spaces serving a particular building shall be located on the shortest accessible route of travel from adjacent parking to an accessible entrance. In parking facilities that do not serve a particular building, accessible parking shall be located on the shortest accessible route of travel to an accessible pedestrian entrance of the parking facility.
2. One in every six accessible off-street parking stalls, but not less than one, shall be served by an accessible aisle of 8'-0" minimum width and shall be signed van accessible. The R7-8b sign shall be mounted below the R99B(CA) plaque or the R99C(CA) sign.
3. In each parking stall, a curb or parking bumper shall be provided if required to prevent encroachment of vehicles over the required width of walkways. Parking stalls shall be so located that persons with disabilities are not compelled to wheel or walk behind parked vehicles other than their own. For more parking bumper requirements, see the Standard Specifications.
4. Parking spaces and access aisles shall be level with surface slopes not exceeding 1.5% in all directions.
5. Table A shall be used to determine the required number of accessible parking stalls in each parking lot or garage.
6. Where Plaque R99B(CA), Sign R99C(CA) or Sign R7-8b are installed, the bottom of the sign or plaque panel shall be a minimum of 7'-0" above the surrounding surface.
7. Curb ramps shall conform to the details shown on Standard Plan A88A.
8. Blue paint, instead of white may be used for marking accessibility aisles in areas where snow may cause white markings to not be visible.
9. The words "NO PARKING", shall be painted in white letters no less than 1'-0" high and located so that it is visible to traffic enforcement officials. See Standard Plan A90B for details of the "NO PARKING" pavement marking.
10. A R100B(CA) sign shall be posted in a conspicuous place at each entrance to off-street parking facilities or immediately adjacent to and visible from each stall. The sign shall include the address where the towed vehicle may be reclaimed and the telephone number of the local traffic law enforcement agency.
11. Where a single (non-van) accessible parking space is provided, the loading and unloading access aisle shall be on the passenger side of the vehicle as the vehicle is going forward into the parking space.
12. Where a van accessible parking space is provided, the loading and unloading access aisle shall be 8'-0" wide minimum, and shall be on the passenger side of the vehicle as the vehicle is going forward into the parking space.
13. Accessible Parking Only Sign shall be Sign R99C(CA) or Sign R99(CA) with Plaque R99B(CA).
Legend: ISA - International Symbol of Accessibility.

title: Accessible Parking On-Street
summary: Two plan layouts of accessible on-street parallel parking: the Conventional detail with a curb ramp and the Restricted Right of Way Width detail with blue painted curb and no ramp. It also shows the NO PARKING pavement marking and the R99, R99B and R99C(CA) signs. Spaces must be at least 20'-0" long and 8'-0" wide.
description:
Conventional (see Note 9): plan of an on-street parallel parking space along the curb, with the sidewalk behind and regular parking spaces on both sides. At the upstream end of the accessible space is an access aisle 5'-0" Min long along the curb and 5'-0" Min deep from the curb, bordered by a 4" blue line with 4" white line diagonals at 3'-0" Max centers (see Note 6) and marked NO PARKING (see Note 7). The accessible space beyond the aisle has its length and width per Note 5. The curb along the aisle is blue painted curb. A curb ramp (see Note 4) with detectable warning surface is built from the aisle into the sidewalk, with a 5'-0" Min unobstructed area beside it, and the curb returns to the sidewalk line at a 1:1 Typ transition. An ISA parking sign (see Note 11) stands at the sidewalk.

Restricted Right of Way Width: plan of an on-street parallel parking space at a street corner with a sidewalk too narrow for a ramp (parallel parking, see Note 10). No curb ramp is used. The curb is painted blue along the accessible space (blue painted curb), with a NO PARKING AS REQUIRED zone along the curb nearest the corner, a regular parking space beyond, and an ISA parking sign (see Note 11) at the sidewalk. The length of the space is per Note 5.

Pavement marking: the words NO PARKING stenciled in two lines, NO above PARKING (see Note 7).

Sign R99(CA): a vertical sign with the ISA and the words PARKING ONLY. Plaque R99B(CA), Sign R99(CA) with Plaque R99B(CA): the plaque reads MINIMUM FINE $250 (see Note 3). Sign R99C(CA): a vertical sign combining ISA, PARKING ONLY and MINIMUM FINE $250 panels (see Note 3).
notes:
1. Parking spaces shall be so located that persons with disabilities are not compelled to wheel or walk behind parked vehicles other than their own.
2. Surface slopes of accessible on-street parking spaces shall be the minimum feasible.
3. Where Plaque R99B(CA) or Sign R99C(CA) are installed, the bottom of the sign or plaque panel shall be a minimum of 7'-0" above the surrounding surface.
4. Curb ramps shall conform to the details shown on Standard Plan A88A.
5. Accessible on-street parking spaces shall not be smaller in length or width than that specified by the local jurisdiction for other parking spaces, but not less than 20'-0" in length and not less than 8'-0" in width.
6. Blue paint, instead of white may be used for marking accessibility aisles in areas where snow may cause white markings to not be visible.
7. The words "NO PARKING", shall be painted in white letters no less than 1'-0" high on a contrasting background and located so that it is visible to traffic enforcement officials. See Standard Plan A24E for square foot area for painting the words "NO PARKING".
8. There shall be no obstructions on the sidewalk adjacent to and for the full length of the parking space, except for the ISA parking sign shown.
9. The Conventional detail should be the primary choice of accessible on-street parking. However, if the sidewalk lacks adequate space to construct a standard curb ramp, the restricted right of way detail should be used.
10. If the Restricted Right of Way Width detail is selected and it conflicts with a bus stop or other uses, this detail may apply to the other end of the block.
11. Accessible Parking Only Sign shall be Sign R99C(CA) or Sign R99(CA) with Plaque R99B(CA).
Legend: ISA - International Symbol of Accessibility.
